edges.description: bmad-sprint-status-path.sh locates the host project's sprint-status.yaml by name; bmad-statusline.sh calls it to read that state and derive phase/next/desync, never from a literal path.

edges.output: Graphify's derived code graph, surfaced as a ready/semantic-pending/missing status
edges.description: bmad-statusline.sh checks for the presence and freshness of graphify-out/graph.json to report the graph=ready/semantic-pending/missing status that gates /bmad-next phases. This is a status surfaced to humans and the loop gate, not an input consumed by bmad-loop-parallel.sh's own overlap check, which reads a separate `surface` field supplied externally through BMAD_PARALLEL_CANDIDATES (see the wave→unit edge below).

edges.output: worker-only mode flag for a wave participant, set by the parallel coordinator
edges.description: When a unit runs as one half of a wave, bmad-loop-parallel.sh sets BMAD_LOOP_WORKER_ONLY=1 and bmad-loop.sh reads it to stop after its own story instead of running close_story (which would race on sprint-status.yaml).

edges.output: local test suite exit status, the closure gate every unit must pass before its story can close
edges.description: close_story() in bmad-loop.sh invokes bmad-test-all.sh (or its BMAD_TEST_ALL override) and only proceeds to push/PR/merge on a passing exit code — real execution evidence, never a unit's own assertion.

edges.output: the diff produced by the unit's implementation, materialized outside the worktree
edges.description: step-04-review.md writes the unit's diff to {diff_file} once and hands reviewers the path (never the diff verbatim), so Blind Hunter, Edge Case Hunter, the Verification Gap Reviewer and the Test Coverage Auditor all read the same materialized output. Reviewers are dispatched by path to a vendored review-prompts/*.md file, never by invoking a skill (BMAD 6.11 #2638/#2642 reverted lens-routing for phase-4 reviewers: the indirection truncated instructions).

anchors.name: local-test-suite
anchors.reason: Closure gate for every story: satisfied only by a real exit code from the discovered test-*.sh/test-*.js suite, never by an agent declaring its own work done.

anchors.name: loop-graph-contract
anchors.reason: The graph contract itself, declared frozen by AD-16: a diff that touches its own node types, edges or width policy is meant to never auto-approve, regardless of diff size. Story 10.4 implemented that enforcement -- whole-file match on this anchor's path (already sufficient for edits to loop-graph.json itself) plus `guards` naming the validator/router code that decides what counts as touching this anchor, so that code can't be weakened without also touching this anchor.

anchors.name: review-policy
anchors.reason: Review panel composition and triage rules, declared frozen by AD-16: a diff that changes who reviews or how findings are classified is meant to always escalate to full review. Enforcement (diff-routed review width) is Story 10.3's scope; this entry only records the invariant for 10.3 to read.

width_policy.cutoff: A candidate story is excluded from a wave's selected group when it shares the same epic as any already-selected story, when it declares any dependency (a non-empty deps field), or when it declares the same non-empty surface value as any already-selected story. select_group() in scripts/bmad-loop-parallel.sh (and selectGroup() in scripts/bmad-wave-plan.js) tries each candidate as a possible anchor, in order; for each anchor it builds forward using only later candidates, adding one only if it survives the three filters against every member already in that attempt, up to min(--parallel, ceiling). It returns the first attempt (by anchor order) that reaches >=2 members -- if the first candidate is incompatible with everyone else, later candidates are retried as fresh anchors instead of giving up. Ceiling is 3 stories.
